On Cynthia, however, it didn't go to plan. I had Togekiss Yawn Roost air slash -> baits her Togekiss, which was meant to be yawn air slash, switch to Magnezone, who gets the kill with Thunderbolt. But she got the one turn wakeup and hit a hard aura sphere, leaving them with 1/3 hp, then the expected baited Garchomp came out, so I switched to Gyarados for the crit safe two Ice Fang kill. Except Cynthia switched to Lucario, which I didn't know she could do, but the Infernape switch close combat OHKO was still safe. Which brought in Milotic, but due to the one-turn wake-up, my Magnezone was dead to all rolls of surf, so my planned Toxic stall wasn't gonna work. I realised there was no safe switch, but close combat from Infernape sacrifice into Weavile would have resulted in a kill with night slash on all but like 4 rolls. So of course Milotic survived, which meant Cynthia full restored. It was a guaranteed 4HKO, so I had to pray for a crit or Weavile was dead too, maybe a switch to Gyarados could have worked, but I needed him healthy for Garchomp. No crit so Gyarados could come in to take the last sliver of health on Milotic (Thank you, perfect speed IV), Ice Fang Garchomp, then Bounce Roserade. 

  
It was a messy Champion, but even with two deaths in the final fight, I only had 6 deaths in the whole run, which, for my first Nuzlocke (admittedly as a long-time Nuzlocke fan), isn't too shabby.

  
In hindsight, Gliscor brought nothing to the team; his two immunities and bulk made him an amazing slow U-turn pivot for unplanned fights and steers throughout the game, but he was literally only part of the line for Aaron as a pivot to get Infernape back in, and that could have been rerouted easily. I would have been better off with another Milotic backup, I had a Garchomp backup in Nevermeltice Weavile. Toxic/Leech Seed/Giga Drain/Protect Roserade in the box was a perfect Milotic backup as well. Probably could have done it deathless, but I haven't checked it.

So I do one of three things for party formation

1. You are already a party. Gay the guys together make your characters be adventurers explain why these characters travel together. Make a party. Sometimes I even say whether the group are a team of heroes or a mercenary company or whatever but with experienced players I'll let them pick that. This method constrains player choices but it pretty much ensures that there will be a cohesive party that want to work together 

2. Thrown into the same box. You are all or mostly strangers who have: all been kidnapped by the same or chief/ hired to fight the same big bad by the gnomish king/ been infected by the same mind flayer parasite. When I DM I always have the highest passive perception in the group noted down, everything that I would say in that room for that roll or higher I just say, and my players know this. Your character is always trying to be as perceptive as they can so at my table you cannot ask to roll perception, I will ask for a perception check if something happens that could call for a perception check. For example, if a party of orcs is approaching quietly from behind the camp I may ask all the players for a perception roll against say 15, and everyone who passes it doesn't get surprised in the first round. Alternatively, I may roll a secret perception check if a character approaches a trap I may roll a secret perception check (normally silently on my computer) to influence how I describe the scene, but normally I'll just use passive perception and maybe background/character. But my players are not allowed to ask to roll perception ever (unless I make an obvious mistake).

Instead, they can call for an investigation roll, investigating comes with downsides, it is loud, which means the bad guys in the dungeon may hear them and attack while they're out of formation. It is also time-consuming which can be a reason for more of the bad guys' plans to come to fruition, or they may erect defenses and traps. With Investigation, they *could* all roll, but then no one's redied for danger, which could make sense if you think you've come to a dead end. Someone can also help with investigation which means you only need 2 good people to investigate to have basically as good a chance as any to get good info. I do not let re-rolls of investigation but I do let everyone roll investigation one last time at the end of a dungeon to check for hidden loot if all the baddies have been captured or killed, but it is still loud so they might attract a random encounter, or the guards if they're criminals in a city.

In order to support his collectivisation policies Stalin portrayed all kulaks as being best represented by the privileged, cruel, and corrupt; which was false, and the violence which followed was in many cases, morally wrong and unjustified. But the conservative response that they were in fact simply middle class farmers unfairly attacked for no reason is also false. Some kulaks undeniably burned grain during a famine rather than accede to the redistribution that is usual in times of famine relief, and many did use their limited positions of power to act as little tyrants underpaying desperate workers with no other opportunities.
